subject: Secure multi-tenant on-prem cluster ops playbook
messages:
From: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@helixmed.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Cho <ben.cho@helixmed.com>
Date: 2029-08-29T16:12:00Z
Subject: Initial intake — multi-tenant on-prem cluster constraints and questions

Hi Stephanie / Laura,

Thanks for taking this on. We want Redwood to run in our private datacenter (single VPC-equivalent overlay), supporting three logical tenant classes (prod, staging, sandbox) with strict data separation and different retention policies. Key asks from our security and compliance teams:

- Network segmentation rules (east-west) to ensure no cross-tenant traffic unless explicitly allowed.
- Egress controls and HTTP proxying for model downloads and OS package updates.
- Storage tiering: encrypted blockstore for prod, high-throughput ephemeral NVMe for model caches, and slower archival for logs.
- Clear rollback plan and cluster isolation steps in case of compromise.

Attached is a rough segmentation diagram and a tenant allocation CSV. Can you confirm what node pool topology you recommend, required node labels/taints, and a minimal set of cluster-level network policies we can start with? Also, what's a realistic cutover duration for a first-phase deployment (prod and staging only)?

Thanks,
Alice
Head of Infrastructure, HelixMed

[attachment: network-segmentation-draft-v1.pdf]

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@helixmed.com>, Ben Cho <ben.cho@helixmed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-08-29T18:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial intake — multi-tenant on-prem cluster constraints and questions

Alice — thanks for the clear list. High level answers up-front, then an attachable ops playbook draft and checklist.

1) Node pool topology (recommended minimal):
   - prod-pool: GPU-enabled nodes (pinned to prod taint), encrypted blockstore (LUKS/KMS), 3 availability racks for fault domain.
   - staging-pool: same as prod but smaller instance count, read-only access to prod snapshots if needed.
   - sandbox-pool: burstable CPU/GPU nodes, ephemeral NVMe with no persistent access to prod volumes.
   - infra-pool: control-plane adjacencies (logging, proxy, monitoring), non-customer workloads.

2) Labels/Taints:
   - node-role=prod + taint redwood/tenant=prod:NoSchedule
   - redwood/ssd-cache=true for NVMe caching nodes
   - redwood/secure-block=true for nodes with attached encrypted blockstore

3) Network & Egress:
   - Default-deny all namespaces; explicit NetworkPolicies per tenant namespace allowing only necessary ports to platform services.
   - Centralized HTTP(S) proxy (infra-pool) for package/model downloads; DNS sinkhole for known-malicious domains.
   - Egress per-tenant allowlists; centralized egress gateway with per-tenant TLS inspection stub (if allowed by compliance).

4) Storage tiers:
   - Prod: encrypted block PVs (RWO) backed by SAN/NVMe RAID, snapshots retained per policy.
   - Model-cache nodes: local NVMe ephemeral caches with controlled prefetching and eviction.
   - Logs/archives: write-through to secure object store, lifecycle rules move older logs to archival.

5) Rollback / isolation playbook (high level):
   - Isolate tenant network at service and node level (cordon/taint nodes + namespace NetworkPolicy deny-all).
   - Snapshot prod volumes; failover traffic to warm standby region or dedicated hot lane if configured.
   - For compromised nodes: scrub and reprovision; preserve audit logs in immutable archive for investigation.

I'm attaching a short ops-playbook draft and a rollout checklist (phase 0 = prod+staging only). Our recommended cutover for phase 0 (greenfield pre-provisioned hardware) is 48–72 hours for an initial cluster with core services, plus 1 week for tenant migrations and policy hardening.

Would you like a Zoom tomorrow to walk through the diagram and the checklist?

—Steph
Steph Nguyen
Manager, Deployment Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2029-08-29T20:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial intake — multi-tenant on-prem cluster constraints and questions

Adding a couple practical notes from delivery:

- Tenant admission: we should require a minimal MVP manifest per tenant listing data residency, retention, and inbound/outbound endpoints. We'll keep a small admission controller validating that.
- CSI choices: prefer LUKS-on-top-of-CSI for block PVs to ensure node-level encryption keys are not mobile; we can integrate with the customer's KMS.
- KV cache: recommend model-layer caching within pod sidecars for LLMs to avoid frequent blockstore hits.

Operational ask for Helix: can you confirm whether the datacenter offers hardware RAID or raw NVMe with software RAID? That determines our PV recommendations.

Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Cho <ben.cho@helixmed.com>

Subject: Re: Initial intake — multi-tenant on-prem cluster constraints and questions

Marissa, Steph — thanks. Data center uses raw NVMe in the hot nodes and offers BMC-managed hardware RAID arrays in the storage racks; we can carve LUNs for block PVs. We'll confirm KMS options tomorrow.

One more ask from our compliance: we need an immutable evidence collection step in the rollback playbook — before reprovisioning, we must capture memory/disk images and push to a tamper-evident archive. Can Redwood include a short routine or recommend tooling?

Ben
Infrastructure Engineering Lead, HelixMed

[attachment: tenant-allocation-table.csv]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Cho <ben.cho@helixmed.com>, Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@helixmed.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-08-30T01:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial intake —multi-tenant on-prem cluster constraints and questions

Ben / Alice — good catch on the evidence collection requirement. Quick proposal to include in the playbook:

1) Isolate node and take a live forensic snapshot (volatility-lite + disk-image) into an encrypted S3-compatible archive (write-once bucket + object-lock).
2) Log collection: ensure auditd/syscalls are forwarded to an append-only store; enable kube-audit and immutable export.
3) Reprovision path: provide an automated ansible/terraform job that reprovisions nodes from golden images and re-attaches PVs only after verification.

I'll add an "Incident containment" appendix to the rollout-checklist with exact commands and a short runbook for the on-call engineer. Estimated update to the playbook: +1 business day.

Rishi Malhotra
Principal SRE — Redwood Inference
